problem_statement: JS→Rust pattern porting risks in 333 Platform: dynamic typing patterns (hot-load extensions) conflict with Rust static typing. 226 Puter upstream services merged without filtration (deprecated code, unused abstractions). Uncritical porting dilutes 333's P2P-first architecture; custom CRDT kept (ADR-006), but broader codebase risks include: over-parameterization, trait bloat from Loro/libp2p integration paths, wasm-bindgen coupling.

key_findings.evidence: ADR-006 analysis shows Loro u64 is cryptographically unbound; cannot replace BFT identity. Any adoption requires side-table identity layer.
key_findings.mitigation: Keep 333 custom CRDT (165× faster, 3× smaller wire). Loro only reconsidered if rich-text or TS-native CRDT becomes product requirement.

key_findings.evidence: 226 Puter services referenced; most are desktop-OS abstractions (file dialogs, system UI) irrelevant to P2P browser. No filtering criteria applied.
key_findings.mitigation: Audit public Puter APIs used by 333 directly. Archive >90% as unused imports. Create minimal abstraction layer for P2P IO (Socket trait only, not MonitoringService/PluginManager/etc).

key_findings.finding: Dynamic typing patterns (extension hooks) unmappable to Rust
key_findings.impact: loss of flexibility without corresponding gain in safety
key_findings.evidence: Puter plugin system expects runtime-reflective registration; Rust requires compile-time trait bounds. Hot-load extension pattern conflicts with wasm-pack/static library model.
key_findings.mitigation: Define static extension registry at compile-time. For future runtime plugins, use Wasm component model (not dynamic .so loading).

key_findings.finding: Solid audit debt (DIP violations in wasm.rs)
key_findings.impact: 8 concrete types coupled; trait abstraction incomplete
key_findings.evidence: apt-progress.md: SPAN_333_SOLID_Refactor underway. PlatformCore trait must replace concrete: bft::HotStuff, crdt::LwwMap, wire::Encoder, tokenomics::333Coin, etc.
key_findings.mitigation: Complete ST/SCW contract mapping (each concrete → trait method). Validate PlatformCore can fully substitute before merging.

key_findings.finding: Performance cliff: Loro 165× slower than custom CRDT
key_findings.impact: frame budget blow (5ms margin already consumed)
key_findings.evidence: Spike result: Loro 6,456µs vs custom 39µs on 3-peer 10-key workload (debug build; ratio holds in release).
key_findings.mitigation: Loro rejected. Custom CRDT kept. Monitor frame latency p95; if <1.5ms margin remaining, profile & optimize CRDT merge or defer BFT to Web Worker.

root_causes: Incomplete upstream codebase audit (226 services → 5-10 actually needed)
No filtering rubric for paradigm mismatch (JS dynamic ↔ Rust static)
Trait abstraction started late (SOLID audit DIP violations discovered in Phase 3)
Performance not measured until integration (Loro spike at SCW, not SA)

recommended_actions.acceptance_criteria: Cargo.lock reports <10 new transitive deps; deleted imports >90%
8/8 concrete → trait mapping verified; unit tests validate substitutability

recommended_actions.action: Lock frame budget: measure p95 latency
Defer complex integration patterns to RC phase
recommended_actions.acceptance_criteria: No new external crate adoptions without spike; hot-reload postponed to v2

summary_300w: 333 Platform faces JS→Rust porting friction: (1) Loro CRDT cannot replace Ed25519 identity without side-table overhead; custom CRDT kept (165× faster). (2) Puter upstream bloat: 226 services merged, 90% unused; pluggable architecture unmappable to static Rust (hot-load extensions ↔ compile-time traits). (3) Solid audit debt: 8 concrete types still coupled in wasm.rs; PlatformCore abstraction must complete before SCW merge. (4) Performance not measured until late: Loro spike revealed 165× latency gap, already frame budget-critical. Mitigations: archive unused imports, validate trait substitutability, lock frame budget <7ms, defer runtime-pluggable patterns to v2 (Wasm component model).
